summary: Webot (formerly Pionex.US) is a cryptocurrency trading platform offering automated trading bots, spot trading, and related services for US users.
systemPrompt:
You are Webot's customer support agent on Telegram. Be warm, concise, and helpful. Respond in the user's language. Plain text only — no markdown, no bold. Use bullet points (- ) for lists. Keep answers short and scannable.

IDENTITY: Our platform is called Webot. Always use "Webot" in your replies — never say "Pionex.US" unless the user specifically asks about it. Pionex.US is our old name (same company, same platform, same accounts). When a user says "Pionex", "Pionex.US", "Pionex US", "Phoenix", "Phoenix.US", "phoenix.us", "Phonex", "Pioneer", "Poinex", or any similar misspelling, they mean OUR platform (Webot). Help them. Never say "Webot and Pionex are separate." The only exception: if they specifically mention "pionex.com" or "Pionex Global", that IS a different company — direct them to pionex.com.

CONFIDENCE: State facts from the FAQ directly. Never add hedging phrases like "if it's supported", "if available", "you may need to check", "the coin may not support this yet". If the FAQ says a feature works for all listed coins, say so. Do not invent caveats or edge cases that are not in the FAQ.

SCOPE: Never offer to do something you cannot actually do. Do not invite follow-up questions you cannot answer (e.g. "send me your budget and I'll suggest parameters" — you have no ability to calculate parameters). Only offer next steps that the user can do themselves in the app, or direct them to human support.

HOW TO ANSWER:
- Use FAQ context as your knowledge source, but write replies in your own words. Do not copy-paste FAQ answers. Keep the key facts accurate but make it sound natural and conversational.
- For simple questions: 2-4 sentences, get to the point.
- For how-to questions: use the FAQ's exact navigation paths (e.g. "Settings icon (top right) → Settings → Notification Settings"). Group by goal: "Step 1 — Enable notifications:" then the path. Do not reorder or merge steps.
- For problems: one empathetic line, then 2-3 likely causes/fixes as bullets. Under 6 lines.
- For greetings: respond warmly, invite them to ask a question.

TOOLS:
- Call webot_check_pair only when the user asks "is X listed?" — not for how-to questions that mention a coin.
- Call webot_list_all_pairs for full coin list requests.
- When reporting listing results, just confirm the pair. Do not mention deposits unless the user asks.

DEPOSITS: When a user asks how to deposit a specific coin, do not give step-by-step deposit instructions. Tell them to check Wallet → Receive Crypto in the app to confirm the deposit channel is open — a coin being listed does not mean deposits are enabled.

HANDOFF: If the question is beyond your knowledge, involves account security, or the user requests a human, set intent to "handoff". Acknowledge their situation briefly and say a human agent can help. Do not include any bot link — it is appended automatically.

DO NOT:
- Guarantee returns or predict prices. However, you CAN help users choose bot parameters (grid range, number of grids, mode) — that is product guidance, not financial advice. Always recommend AI Strategy as the easiest option.
- When your answer involves trading strategies, bot parameters, or any investment-related guidance, end your reply with: "This is not financial advice. Trading involves risk — only invest what you can afford to lose."
- Comment on taxes, legal, regulatory, or compliance matters
- Accept or ask for passwords, private keys, seed phrases, or 2FA codes
- Send external links
- Make promises about timelines, refunds, or compensation
- Refer to personal staff — only https://t.me/webot_cs_bot for human support

RESPONSE FORMAT: Output a single JSON object only. No extra text.
{"intent": "answer" or "handoff", "reply": "<your response>", "faq_id": "<id of the FAQ you based your answer on, or null if none>", "show_images": true or false}

faqs.question: What is Webot?
faqs.answer:
Webot (formerly Pionex.US) is a US-based cryptocurrency trading platform offering automated trading bots, spot trading, and portfolio management tools for US users.

Webot is the rebranded version of Pionex.US — same platform, same account. You can log in with your Pionex.US credentials on Webot. All new features go to Webot only.

Note: Pionex (the global exchange at pionex.com) is a separate company. We cannot assist with Pionex Global accounts.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Pionex and Webot?
faqs.answer:
Pionex.US and Webot are the SAME platform — Webot is the official brand upgrade of Pionex.US.

- Same account, same login credentials — log in with your Pionex.US email and password
- Your funds, bots, and trading history are synced between both apps in real time
- All new features and updates go to Webot only (e.g. improved fiat deposit, new AI tools, 2025 tax reports)
- The Pionex.US app still works but will no longer receive new features or maintenance
- We recommend switching to Webot for the best experience

Note: Pionex.US and Webot are now two separate apps. Download Webot from the App Store or Google Play.

However, Pionex Global (pionex.com) is a completely separate company. We cannot help with Pionex Global accounts — contact them at pionex.com.

faqs.question: What trading bots are available?
faqs.answer:
Webot offers the following trading bots:
1. Grid Trading Bot – buy low, sell high within a price range. Best for sideways markets.
2. Reverse Grid Bot – accumulates base currency by selling high and buying back lower. Best for bear markets.
3. Martingale (DCA) Bot – ladder-buys on dips, sells all at once on rebound. Reduces average holding cost.
4. Rebalancing Bot – maintains a balanced portfolio ratio across multiple coins.
5. Smart Trade Bot – one-time trade with take-profit and stop-loss settings. Best for trending markets.
6. BTC & ETH Moon Bot – pre-configured grid strategy for BTC or ETH.
7. TWAP Bot – splits large orders over time to reduce market impact.

Past performance does not guarantee future results.

faqs.question: How does the Grid Trading Bot work?
faqs.answer:
The Grid Trading Bot automatically buys low and sells high within a set price range, generating grid profits from market fluctuations. It runs 24/7.

Key parameters:
- Upper/Lower limit: The price range the bot operates in. Bot pauses if price goes outside this range.
- Number of grids: More grids = more frequent trades but smaller profit per trade.
- Investment: Minimum investment is calculated based on your range and grid count.
- Grid mode: Arithmetic (equal intervals) or Geometric (proportional intervals).

Advanced: Trigger price, stop loss, take profit, slippage control, trailing up.

Best for: Sideways or volatile markets. Use AI Strategy if you're unsure of parameters.

How to create (App): Bot → Create → Grid Trading Bot → Choose pair → Set parameters or use AI Strategy → Create → OK.
How to create (Web): Trade → Trading Bot → Bot → All → Grid Trading Bot → Choose pair → Set parameters → Create Bot → Continue.

faqs.question: How does the Reverse Grid Bot work?
faqs.answer:
The Reverse Grid Bot accumulates base currency (e.g. ETH) by selling at high prices and buying back at lower prices. Unlike the regular Grid Bot which measures profit in quote currency (USDT), the Reverse Grid measures profit in base currency (ETH).

Best for: Bear markets or when you want to grow your coin holdings.

Key parameters:
- Upper/Lower limit: Operating price range.
- Grids: Number of price levels.
- Investment: Amount of base currency (tokens) to invest.
- Stop loss: Triggered when price rises (converts USDT back to base currency).
- Take profit: Triggered when price falls enough (converts USDT back to base currency).

Note: After stop loss or take profit, the bot converts all USDT back to base currency.

How to create (App): Bot → Create → Reverse Grid Bot → Choose pair → Set parameters → Create → OK.
How to create (Web): Trade → Trading Bot → Bot → All → Reverse Grid Bot → Choose pair → Set parameters → Create Bot → Continue.

faqs.question: How does the Martingale (DCA) Bot work?
faqs.answer:
The Martingale Bot ladder-buys on price dips and sells everything at once when the price rebounds to your take-profit level. It uses increasing order sizes (1x, 2x, 4x, 8x...) to reduce average holding cost.

Best for: Coins with good long-term fundamentals. Best started at a non-high price.

Key parameters:
- Price scale: The % drop that triggers each additional buy.
- Take profit ratio: The % rebound at which the bot sells all coins.
- Investment: Total amount to invest.
- Safety orders: Number of dip-buying levels.
- Volume scale: Multiplier for each successive buy order.

The bot automatically reinvests profits into the next round (auto-compounding).

Martingale vs Grid: Martingale has lower risk and higher arbitrage profit in volatile markets; Grid has higher trend profit when market rises steadily.

How to create (App): Bot → Create → Martingale Bot → Standard Mode → Choose pair → AI Strategy or set manually → Create → Confirm.
How to create (Web): Trade → Trading Bot → Bot → All → Martingale Bot → Choose pair → Use AI Strategy → Create → OK.

faqs.question: How does the Rebalancing Bot (屯币宝) work?
faqs.answer:
The Rebalancing Bot maintains a target allocation ratio across multiple coins by automatically buying and selling when prices shift. For example, a 1:1 BTC/ETH portfolio will be rebalanced whenever one coin outperforms the other.

Modes:
- Dual-coin: Balances 2 coins at a 1:1 ratio.
- Multi-coin: Balances up to 10 coins with custom ratios.

Rebalancing methods:
- Periodic: Rebalances at set time intervals (e.g. every 4 or 24 hours).
- Threshold: Rebalances when any coin deviates beyond a set % from target.

Minimum investment: 10 USDT per coin (e.g. 2 coins = 20 USDT minimum).
Trading fee: 0.1% per rebalance transaction.

How to create (App): Bot → Create → Rebalancing Bot → Choose mode and coins → Enter investment → Create → Confirm.
How to create (Web): Trade → Trading Bot → Bot → All → Rebalancing Bot → Choose coins → Set parameters → Create → OK.

faqs.question: How does the Smart Trade Bot work?
faqs.answer:
Smart Trade lets you schedule a buy with automatic take-profit and stop-loss, running 24/7 without manual monitoring.

Modes:
- Limit (Standard): Set a specific buy price, take-profit price, and stop-loss price.
- Market (Speed): Use when you want to chase an uptrend immediately. Set investment amount and trailing percentage only.

Take-profit options:
- Fixed-Price: Sells when price reaches your set target.
- Trailing Take-Profit: Activates at a trigger price, then sells when price drops from its peak by the trailing %.

Stop-loss: Set the price at which the bot closes. Set to 0 to disable.

Best for: Trending or volatile markets when you want to capture a move with defined risk.

How to create (App): Bot → Create → Smart Trade → Choose pair → Select mode → Set buy price, take profit, stop loss → Create.
How to create (Web): Trade → Trading Bot → Bot → All → Smart Trade → Choose pair → Set parameters → Create.

faqs.question: How do I set up Auto-Reinvestment on the Grid Trading Bot?
faqs.answer:

Web: Open your Grid Bot → Settings → Auto-Reinvestment → Enable.

faqs.question: How does the BTC & ETH Moon Bot (BTC天地单 / ETH天地单) work?
faqs.answer:
BTC/ETH Moon Bot is a pre-configured grid trading strategy for BTC or ETH. Parameters are automatically set based on current market prices — no manual configuration needed.

It runs 24/7, capturing grid profits from price fluctuations. Grid profits can be withdrawn at any time.

Total profit = Grid profit + Unrealized profit (trend gains from price increase).

How to create (App): Bot → Create → Strategy → Select BTC Moon or ETH Moon → Choose USD or USDT → Enter investment → Continue.
How to create (Web): Trade → Trading Bot → Strategy → Select BTC Moon or ETH Moon → Choose USD or USDT → Enter investment → Create.

Note: Investment amount cannot be changed after the bot is created. Parameters cannot be modified while running.

App step 2: Choose USD or USDT → Enter investment amount → Continue
Web step 1: Go to Trade → Trading Bot → Strategy → Select BTC Moon or ETH Moon
Web step 2: Choose USD or USDT → Enter investment amount → Create

faqs.question: How does the TWAP Bot (定投机器人) work?
faqs.answer:
TWAP (Time-Weighted Average Price) splits a large order into smaller equal-sized orders executed at regular time intervals. This reduces market impact and achieves a better average price.

Parameters:
- Order period: 10 sec, 30 sec, 1 min, or 5 min.
- Buy/Sell amount per order: Amount to trade each interval.
- Total transactions: Number of times to repeat.

Example: Buy 1,000 USDT of ETH every 10 seconds, 100 times = 100,000 USDT total.

How to use (Web): Trade → Trading Bot → TWAP → Select pair → Set order period, amount per order, and number of transactions → Start.

faqs.question: Why is my ACH deposit still pending?
faqs.answer: ACH deposits require time to process through bank settlement. Even if your bank shows the payment was deducted, it can take up to 4 business days for Webot to receive and confirm the transfer. The order status will remain 'pending' during this time. If the status doesn't update after 4 business days, contact support at service@webot.com.

faqs.question: Why can't I withdraw my recently deposited funds? When will my ACH deposit be available?
faqs.answer:
ACH deposits take up to 4 business days to be credited to your Webot account after your bank deducts the funds. This is normal — your bank sends the money but Webot does not receive it until the bank settlement clears.

Once credited, there is a holding period before you can withdraw to your bank:
- Bank Account (ACH): 14 days from the credit date
- Debit Card: 10 days from the credit date
- Wire Transfer: 24 hours from the credit date

Note: The hold starts from when the deposit is credited to your Webot account, not from when your bank deducts the funds.

To check your exact withdrawable date: Home → Deposit → History → tap the deposit → Withdrawable Time.

If your funds are still unavailable after the hold period, contact support at service@webot.com.

faqs.question: What is 3D Secure (3DS) and how to complete it?
faqs.answer:
3DS is a security verification required for debit card deposits. When prompted:
- Challenge flow: Enter the PIN or one-time passcode sent by your bank
- Frictionless flow: Wait 2-3 seconds, the page auto-redirects

Common reasons 3DS fails:
- Your card issuer does not support 3DS
- Your bank blocks crypto exchange payments
- Verification code not entered within 15 minutes

If 3DS keeps failing, contact your bank or try a different card.

faqs.question: How do I avoid investment scams?
faqs.answer:
Crypto transactions are irreversible. If you send crypto to a scammer, it cannot be recovered.

Common scam types: Ponzi schemes, pyramid schemes, fake high-return investments.

Red flags:
- Promises of high returns with no risk
- Pressure to bring in more people
- Grammar errors in communications
- Unverifiable organizations

If you suspect a scam, report it to:
- SEC: investor.gov
- FTC: consumer.ftc.gov
- Your state's securities regulator

Webot will never ask you to send funds to a third party for 'investment management'.

faqs.question: Why is my deposited crypto not showing in my available balance?
faqs.answer:
Don't worry — this is normal and your funds are safe! There are two balance types on Webot:

- Total Balance: Shows all your assets including recently deposited funds that are still being confirmed.
- Available Balance: Only shows funds that are fully cleared and ready to trade or withdraw.

Here are the common reasons your deposit may not appear in Available Balance yet:

1. Waiting for blockchain confirmations — crypto deposits require a certain number of block confirmations before they are credited. This varies by coin and network traffic.
2. Holding period — USD deposits have a holding period (ACH: 14 days, Debit Card: 10 days, Wire: 24 hours) before they become available for withdrawal.
3. Deposit channel under maintenance — if the coin's deposit channel is temporarily under maintenance, crediting may be delayed until maintenance is complete.

To check your deposit status: App → Home → Deposit → History.

If your deposit has been confirmed on the blockchain but still hasn't appeared after a reasonable time, please contact support at https://t.me/webot_cs_bot.

faqs.question: What are the trading fees on Webot?
faqs.answer:
Webot charges the following spot trading fees:

- Taker fee: 0.5% per trade
- Maker fee: 0.1% per trade

Taker vs Maker explained:
- Taker: You place a market order that fills immediately from existing orders in the book.
- Maker: You place a limit order that sits in the order book and gets filled later.

Fees are deducted automatically from the proceeds of your trade — you do not need to deposit extra funds to cover them. For example, if you sell 100 USDT worth of BTC as a taker, you receive 99.5 USDT after the 0.5% fee.

For crypto withdrawal fees, those are separate and charged per withdrawal. You can check crypto withdrawal fees in the Webot app or ask me about a specific coin.

faqs.question: How do I set up a price alert on Webot?
faqs.answer:
Price alerts are available in the Webot mobile app and the Pionex.US mobile app. This feature is NOT available on the web version. Any coin listed on Webot can have a price alert set up.

On the Webot app:
Step 1 — Enable notifications: Tap the Settings icon (top right) → Settings → Notification Settings → turn on Custom Alert
Step 2 — Set a price alert: Home → Search icon (bottom right) → search for the coin → Bell icon (top right) → set your target price (above or below) → create alert

Make sure your phone's notification permission for the app is also turned on.

(If the user is on the Pionex.US app, give these steps instead: Step 1 — Account → Settings → Notification Settings → enable Custom Alert. Step 2 — Search Coin → Bell icon → set target price → create alert. Only mention Pionex.US steps if the user specifically asks about the Pionex.US app. If the user says they can't find it on web, tell them it's mobile app only.)

faqs.question: What will the listing price be? What do you think about the price?
faqs.answer:
That's a question a lot of people are curious about! However, Webot does not comment on price predictions, price targets, or expected price movements for any asset.

Crypto markets are highly volatile and prices are determined by supply and demand — no one can predict them with certainty. Making price predictions could also be considered financial advice, which we are not licensed to provide.

For market data and price information, you can check platforms like CoinMarketCap or CoinGecko. For trading decisions, please do your own research and consider your personal risk tolerance.

Remember: never invest more than you can afford to lose.

faqs.question: Why are deposits or withdrawals suspended for a coin?
faqs.answer:
From time to time, deposits or withdrawals for a specific coin may be temporarily suspended. This is usually due to:

- Wallet maintenance or upgrades on Webot's end
- Network upgrades or hard forks on the coin's blockchain
- Security reviews

What you should do:
- Do NOT send funds to a Webot deposit address while deposits are suspended. If you send during maintenance, your funds may not be credited until maintenance is complete, or in some cases may be delayed indefinitely.
- Wait for an official announcement in the Webot community or app before sending.
- Already sent? If you sent before the suspension was announced and the blockchain confirms the transaction, your funds will typically be credited once maintenance is complete. Please contact support at https://t.me/webot_cs_bot if you need help.

We always announce maintenance windows in advance when possible. Follow the official Webot channels for updates.

faqs.question: Can I deposit BLESS on Webot?
faqs.answer:
BLESS is listed for trading on Webot (BLESS/USD and BLESS/USDT pairs), but BLESS deposits are not yet available. Only trading is supported at this time.

We will announce when BLESS deposits open. Stay tuned to official Webot channels for updates.

faqs.question: How do I link a bank account to Webot?
faqs.answer: To link a bank account to Webot, go to your account settings and select the Wallet or Payment Methods section. From there, you can add a bank account by entering your routing number and account number. Webot uses ACH to verify your bank account, which may involve small test deposits or instant verification through your online banking credentials. Once verified, you can use your bank account to deposit or withdraw USD. Please note that only US-based bank accounts are supported at this time.

faqs.question: My KYC verification was rejected. What should I do?
faqs.answer: If your KYC verification was rejected, do not worry. This can happen for a few common reasons, such as a blurry or incomplete document photo, an expired ID, or a mismatch between your submitted information and your official documents. Here is what you can do: First, review any rejection email or notification you received, as it will often indicate the reason. Then, return to the KYC section in your account and resubmit with a clear, well-lit photo of a valid government-issued ID and make sure all details match exactly. If you continue to have trouble, please reach out to our support team and we will be happy to help you resolve it.

faqs.question: How many block confirmations are required for a BDAG deposit?
faqs.answer: BDAG deposits on Webot require a certain number of block confirmations before the funds are credited to your account. Block confirmation requirements help ensure the security and finality of transactions on the network. The exact number of required confirmations for BDAG may vary and can be subject to change. You can typically find the current confirmation requirement displayed on the deposit page for BDAG within the Webot app or platform. If your deposit is taking longer than expected, you can use the transaction ID (TXID) to check the current confirmation status on a blockchain explorer. If the required confirmations have been met and your balance has still not updated, please contact our support team.

faqs.question: Can I have multiple accounts on Webot?
faqs.answer: No, each person is only permitted to have one account on Webot. Our terms of service require that every account is tied to a unique individual identity, which is verified through our KYC process. Creating multiple accounts is not allowed and may result in the suspension or closure of all associated accounts. If you are having trouble accessing your existing account, please use the password reset option or contact our support team for assistance.

faqs.question: How do I delete my Webot account?
faqs.answer:
To delete your Webot account, you must first withdraw all funds from your account. Please note that account deletion is permanent and cannot be reversed. Once your balance reaches zero, you can submit a deletion request through:

Website: Hover over your profile photo, then go to Account Settings > Delete Account
App: Go to Account > Settings > Profile > Delete Account

If you need additional assistance, please contact our support team. They will help verify your identity and guide you through the process. Please keep in mind that deleting your account will permanently remove access to your trading history, and the process may take a few business days to complete.

Keywords: delete account, close account, remove account, deactivate account, account deletion
Sources: How do I delete my Webot account?

faqs.question: Which crypto tokens can I deposit and withdraw on Webot?

BTC (Bitcoin) | USDT (ERC20, TRC20, BEP20) | ETH (ERC20, BASE) | AAVE | ADA | ALGO | APE | ATOM | AVAX | AXS | BCH | BDAG | BNB | COMP | CRV | DOGE | ETC | FIL | FTM | GALA | GRT | IMX | IP | KAS | LINK | LTC | MANA | OP | POL | SHIB | SOL | UNI | USDC (ERC20, Solana, BASE) | XRP | XLM | YFI and more.

faqs.question: What is a Memo or Destination Tag and do I need it?
faqs.answer:
Some cryptocurrencies require both an address AND a Memo (or Destination Tag) to receive funds correctly. The address routes funds to Webot, while the Memo ensures they are credited to your specific account. Think of the address as a building street address, and the Memo as your apartment number — both are needed.

Tokens that commonly require a Memo on Webot: ATOM, XLM, XRP, EOS.

If you send funds to a Memo-required address without including the Memo, your funds may be lost. Always check the deposit page for your specific token on Webot to confirm if a Memo is required before sending.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Pionex.US and Webot?
faqs.answer:
Webot is the official brand upgrade of Pionex.US, built to provide a better experience for US users. No re-registration is needed — you can log in to Webot with your existing Pionex.US email and password. Your funds, positions, trading history, and referral codes are automatically synced.

Key differences: New features like 2025 tax reports and SSN/TIN updates are available exclusively on Webot. Future updates will be released on Webot only. The Pionex.US and Webot web platforms are currently functionally identical.

Webot is an officially certified Money Services Business (MSB) with NMLS ID: 2284360, available across 47 US states + US Virgin Islands.

faqs.question: How do I convert small coin balances to USDT on Webot?
faqs.answer:
Small coin balances that are too small to trade can be converted to USDT directly in the Webot app.

App: Go to [Assets] and look for the option to convert small balances. Select the coins you want to convert and confirm.

This is useful for cleaning up dust balances left over after trading. Note that the converted amount may be slightly lower than market price due to conversion fees.

faqs.question: I am not receiving the email verification code. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
If you are not receiving the email verification code, try these steps:

1. Check your spam or junk folder — verification emails sometimes end up there.
2. Make sure you entered the correct email address.
3. Wait a few minutes and request a new code — there may be a short delay.
4. Add no-reply@webot.com to your contacts or whitelist to prevent future filtering.
5. If your inbox is full, delete some emails and try again.

If none of the above works, please contact our support team at https://t.me/webot_cs_bot.

faqs.question: How do I find my referral or invitation link on Webot?
faqs.answer:
To find your referral link on Webot:

App: Tap your profile icon → [Invite Friends] or [Referral]. Your unique invitation link and code will be displayed there.

Web: Log in → click your avatar → [Invite Friends].

You can share your referral link to earn commission when your friends trade on Webot.

faqs.question: My 1099-DA shows a much larger amount than what I invested. Is it wrong?
faqs.answer:
Your 1099-DA is most likely correct. Here is why the numbers may look larger than expected:

1099-DA reports your total gross proceeds — the combined value of every sale or trade you made during the year. It does NOT show your profit or loss.

Example: If you invested $1,000 and your trading bot made 500 trades throughout the year, the 1099-DA may show $50,000+ in proceeds because it adds up every single trade, not just your starting amount.

To calculate your actual profit or loss for tax year 2025:
- Profit/Loss = Total Proceeds minus Total Cost Basis
- Cost basis is what you originally paid for the crypto you sold
- The IRS does not require exchanges to report cost basis on 1099-DA for tax year 2025, so you need to calculate it yourself or use tax software

Webot provides a Profit & Loss report you can download from the Tax Report section. Please review it carefully and cross-check with your own records, as bot trading activity can produce complex transaction histories. If the numbers still seem off after reviewing, contact support at service@webot.com.

faqs.question: I cannot find my 2025 tax report or 1099. Where is it?
faqs.answer:
Your 2025 tax report (including 1099-DA) is only available on Webot, not on the old Pionex.US app.

To access it:
1. Log in to the Webot app or webot.com
2. Go to Profile → Tax Report
3. Select tax year 2025

Your Webot login credentials are the same as your Pionex.US account — no new account needed.

For transaction history from before the migration (2024 and earlier), some data may only be accessible through Pionex.US. If you need help locating historical records, contact support at service@webot.com.

faqs.question: Why is the BDAG price on Webot much lower than on other platforms?
faqs.answer:
The price difference is due to liquidity. BDAG is a low-liquidity token, meaning there are few buyers and sellers actively trading it.

Other platforms may show a higher price but have restricted deposits or withdrawals for BDAG, which traps liquidity and inflates the displayed price. On Webot, BDAG trades in an open market where the price is determined purely by actual buy and sell orders.

This is not a platform error or manipulation. The price you see on Webot reflects real tradeable value at the current market depth.

faqs.question: What documents do I need for identity verification?
faqs.answer:
Webot accepts the following documents for KYC:

Government-issued ID (one of):
- U.S. State Driver's License (front and back)
- U.S. Passport (information page)
- Federal/State-issued ID card (front and back)

SSN or TIN is also required.

Proof of Address — only required if verifying with a Passport. Accepted documents: utility bills, bank/credit card statements, mortgage statements (dated within last 6 months).

Tips for success:
- Use original physical documents, not photocopies or screenshots
- Ensure photos are clear, well-lit, fully visible
- Complete verification on the Webot mobile app for best results

If rejected without a clear reason, contact support at @webot_cs_bot.

faqs.question: Can I use SMS instead of Google Authenticator for verification?

Yes — Webot supports 3 verification methods:

- SMS (text message) code
- Google Authenticator (recommended)

All 3 may be required for withdrawals depending on what's enabled on your account.

If you're not receiving SMS codes:
- Make sure you're not using an authenticator app (they don't send SMS)

- After too many resend attempts, SMS is temporarily blocked for 24 hours

Lost your phone number or email access? Submit an unbind request: https://forms.gle/2ynPFuTAjTNsocfCA (processed within 3 business days). Note: withdrawals are restricted for 72 hours after unbinding.

faqs.question: How do I change my phone number on my account?
faqs.answer:
To change your phone number, you need to unbind the old one first — but you must have at least one other verification method (email) still bound to your account before you can unbind your phone.

On the app:
App → Avatar → Security → Multi-factor authentication → select Phone → Unbind

On the web:
Website → Avatar → Account Settings → select Phone → Unbind

Once unbound, follow the same path to add your new phone number.

If you've lost access to all verification methods, contact @webot_cs_bot with your Webot UID for manual assistance.

faqs.question: How do I reset or change my password?
faqs.answer:

App → Account → Forgot password? → Enter your email → Complete CAPTCHA → Enter Google Authenticator code → Enter email/SMS code → Set new password

On the web:
Website → Sign in → Forgot password? → Enter phone or email → Complete CAPTCHA → Enter Google Authenticator code → Enter email/SMS code → Set new password

Note: withdrawals are suspended for 24 hours after a password reset for security reasons.

Having trouble receiving verification codes or Google Authenticator errors? Contact @webot_cs_bot for assistance.

faqs.question: Why is my QR code invalid when logging in on desktop?
faqs.answer:
The QR code on the sign-in page is only valid for 2 minutes. If it expires before you scan it, click Refresh to generate a new one.

To log in via QR code:
1. Go to the Webot sign-in page — a QR code will appear automatically
2. Open the Webot mobile app → tap the QR scan icon in the top right corner of the Home screen
3. Scan the QR code on your browser
4. Tap Authorize in the app

If the issue persists, try clearing your browser cache or use a different browser. Contact @webot_cs_bot if you still can't log in.

faqs.question: My account is linked to an old email I no longer have access to. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
You can unbind your old email as long as you still have at least one other verification method (phone number or Google Authenticator) linked to your account.

If you're still logged in:
App → Avatar → Security → Multi-factor authentication → select Email → Unbind
Web → Avatar → Account Settings → select Email → Unbind

If you've lost access and can't receive the verification code:
Submit an unbind request: https://forms.gle/2ynPFuTAjTNsocfCA
Webot will process it within 3 business days and notify you by email.

Note: withdrawals are restricted for 72 hours after unbinding.

Once unbound, add your new email through the same path.

faqs.question: What happens when my grid bot goes out of range?
faqs.answer:
When the market price moves outside your grid's price range, the bot temporarily pauses — it does not get closed or lose your funds.

- Price goes above upper limit: All assets have been sold. The bot waits and resumes buying once the price drops back into range.
- Price goes below lower limit: Your investment is fully in the base currency (100% position). The bot resumes selling once the price rises back into range.

The bot will automatically resume trading once the price re-enters the defined range — no action needed.

Tip: To protect against large drops, set a Stop-Loss price in Advanced Settings when creating the bot.

faqs.question: How do I set up auto-reinvest on my grid bot?
faqs.answer:
The auto-reinvest function automatically takes your grid profits every 24 hours and reinvests them back into the bot once they reach a minimum threshold.

To enable it: App → Bot → Go to your Bot card → More → Profits Reinvest. This will enable the bot to reinvest your current profit and also auto reinvest future profit.

How it works:
- Grid profits accumulate in a "Reinvesting" section every 24 hours
- Once profits reach the minimum threshold, the bot buys positions at market price and adds them to the grid's sell orders
- After reinvestment, the profits appear in your "Holding profit" section

Important notes:
- Once profits move to the "Reinvesting" section, they cannot be manually released even if you turn off auto-reinvest
- Reinvested profits become part of your principal — if the price drops, temporary losses can occur
- All funds (including reinvested amounts) are returned when you close the bot

faqs.question: Which bot is best for beginners?
faqs.answer:
For beginners, we recommend the Grid Trading Bot with AI Strategy or the BTC/ETH Moon Bot.

Grid Bot (AI Strategy) — easiest to start:
- Select Moderate or Aggressive mode — parameters are automatically set by AI based on historical data
- Just enter your investment amount and the bot handles everything
- App → Bot → Create → Grid Trading Bot → choose Moderate or Aggressive

BTC/ETH Moon Bot — great for long-term holders:
- Pre-configured for BTC or ETH, no parameter adjustments needed
- Best for users who believe in long-term crypto growth
- App → Bot → Create → Strategy → BTC Moon or ETH Moon

Both bots run 24/7 automatically. You can withdraw grid profits at any time without closing the bot.

⚠️ Risk disclaimer: Crypto trading carries significant risk. Bot performance is based on historical data and does not guarantee future results. Only invest what you can afford to lose.

faqs.question: Can I trade immediately after making a deposit?
faqs.answer:
It depends on your deposit method:

- Debit Card: Available to trade instantly. Available to withdraw 10 days after credited.
- ACH (Bank): Available to trade after 0-4 business days. Available to withdraw 14 days after credited.
- Wire Transfer: Available to trade after 1-5 business days. Available to withdraw 24 hours after credited.

Once funds are credited to your account you can trade immediately, but withdrawals are subject to the holding period above.

To check your deposit status:
App → Home → Deposit → History
Web → Orders → Deposit USD Orders

faqs.question: I deposited an unsupported token or used the wrong network. What do I do?
faqs.answer:
If you deposited a token that is not supported on Webot, or sent crypto via the wrong network, please contact @webot_cs_bot immediately with:
- Your Webot UID

⚠️ Important: Sending crypto via the wrong network may result in permanent loss of funds. Webot cannot guarantee recovery in all cases. Always double-check the network before sending.

To avoid this:
App → Home → three dot symbol → Send & Receive → select the correct coin → select the correct network before copying the deposit address.

Web → Wallet → Receive Crypto → select the correct coin → select the correct network before copying the deposit address.

faqs.question: Why can't I deposit or withdraw a specific coin on Webot?
faqs.answer:
There are a few reasons a coin may not be available for deposit or withdrawal:

1. Not listed on Webot — not all coins are supported. You can check the full list of supported coins:
   App → Home → three dot symbol → Send & Receive → search for the coin
   Web → Wallet → Receive Crypto → search for the coin

2. Wallet under maintenance — the deposit/withdrawal channel for that coin may be temporarily suspended. Check the Webot announcements channel for updates.

3. Network not supported — Webot supports specific networks per coin. Make sure you're selecting a supported network.

If the coin is listed but deposits/withdrawals are still not working, contact @webot_cs_bot with your Webot UID and the coin name.

faqs.question: Why do I need to submit a bank statement to withdraw USD?
faqs.answer:
Webot requires a proof of bank account ownership to verify that the receiving account belongs to you. This is a regulatory compliance requirement.

Accepted documents (must clearly show your full name and bank account number):
- Bank statement
- Bank credentials page
- Official letter from the bank

Important rules:
- Bank account must match your Webot KYC name exactly
- Joint accounts and third-party recipients are not supported
- Minimum withdrawal amount is $50 USD
- Withdrawals are processed within 3-7 business days

To withdraw USD:
App → Home → three dot symbol → Withdraw → select method
Web → Wallet → Withdraw USD → select method

faqs.question: Can I deposit or withdraw PI on Webot?
faqs.answer: Yes — PI deposits and withdrawals are fully enabled on Webot. You can deposit PI to your Webot wallet and withdraw PI to an external wallet. Find the deposit address under Wallet → Receive Crypto, and initiate withdrawals from Wallet → Send Crypto.

faqs.question: How do grid bot fees work and how is profit calculated?
faqs.answer:
Grid bots earn profit through the spread between buy and sell orders. Each completed buy-sell cycle generates a grid profit.

Fees: Maker fee is 0.1%, taker fee is 0.5% per trade, deducted from each order.

Profit estimate: Each grid captures the price difference between adjacent grid levels, minus fees on each side. More grids = more frequent trades but smaller profit per trade. Fewer grids = bigger profit per trade but trades less often.

You can see your total grid profit and estimated APR in the bot details screen.

faqs.question: I created a grid bot with old parameters. Can I update them?
faqs.answer:
Yes — you can edit a running grid bot's parameters (such as upper/lower limits, take profit, stop loss, and trailing up) from the bot details screen.

The AI Strategy only suggests parameters when you first create the bot. If the market has moved, you can manually adjust the parameters or stop the bot and create a new one with fresh AI recommendations.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right parameters for a Grid Trading Bot?
faqs.answer:
The easiest way is to use AI Strategy — it sets the price range and grid count automatically based on recent market data.

To create with AI Strategy: Bot → Create → Grid Trading Bot → Select your pair → Choose AI Strategy → Pick Conservative, Moderate, or Aggressive → Set your investment amount → Create.

If you prefer manual setup:
- Price range: Look at the coin's recent trading range (e.g. 7-day or 30-day high/low). Set your upper and lower limits to cover the range you expect the price to stay within.
- Number of grids: 50-100 grids is common for most setups. More grids = more frequent but smaller trades. Fewer grids = larger profit per trade but less frequent.
- Grid mode: Arithmetic for stable ranges, Geometric for volatile markets or wide ranges.
- Investment: The app calculates the minimum based on your range and grid count. Investing more lets each grid order be larger.

Tip: Start with AI Strategy on Moderate if you're unsure — you can always adjust the parameters later from the bot details screen.

faqs.question: My ACH deposit history is empty or I did not receive a confirmation. What happened?
faqs.answer:
If your ACH deposit is not showing:
- App: Deposit → History → Bank Account
- Web: Orders → Deposit USD orders → Bank Account → ACH (Stripe)

ACH deposits typically take 3-5 business days to fully settle and may show as pending during that time.

Note the Withdrawable Time shown on the deposit — ACH funds cannot be withdrawn until that date (standard fraud prevention hold).

If still missing after 5 business days, contact support via @webot_cs_bot.

faqs.question: I signed up for Pionex Global instead of Webot by mistake. Can I get a refund?
faqs.answer:
Webot (formerly Pionex.US) and Pionex Global (pionex.com) are two completely separate companies. If you created an account on Pionex Global by mistake, contact Pionex support at pionex.com — Webot cannot access Pionex Global accounts.

Note: If you signed up on Pionex.US, that IS Webot — same platform, same account. You can log in at webot.com with the same credentials.

faqs.question: What 2FA methods does Webot support?
faqs.answer:
Webot supports three 2FA methods:

- Google Authenticator (recommended, most secure): Generates a time-based one-time code. Not tied to your phone number, resistant to SIM-swap attacks.
- SMS/Text (less secure): Code sent to your phone. Vulnerable to phone number porting attacks.
- Email (less secure): Code sent to your registered email.

Set up Google Authenticator under Account → Security → Google Authenticator. Strongly recommended for withdrawals and login.
